title: Why we’re watching these climate tech companies
gist: Casey Crownhart's newsletter draws three themes from MIT Technology Review's 2026 Climate Tech Companies to Watch: China's dominance in energy technology, Big Tech data-center demand pulling in US firms like Fervo and X-energy, and storage becoming essential to the grid via Form Energy, Energy Dome and Moment Energy.

themes.theme: China at the center of energy tech

insights.claim: China's dominance in energy technology is a persistent global trend: it has the world's largest grid and is adding renewables faster than the author can comprehend.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Chinese scale in renewables continues to set the pace for global clean-energy supply chains.
insights.quote: China is home to the world’s largest grid, and renewables are coming online more quickly than I can wrap my head around.
insights.locator: China is the center of the climate and energy tech world

insights.claim: Envision Energy, on the list for the second time, has installed over 100 GW of wind and over 50 GWh of battery storage worldwide, and is expanding abroad to Germany, Brazil, Australia and soon Vietnam as the Chinese market gets crowded.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Chinese renewables majors are exporting capacity as domestic competition intensifies.
insights.locator: Contributing to that boom is Envision Energy

insights.claim: Chinese firms are racing to develop solid-state batteries; WeLion achieved 824 Wh/kg in a lab result last year, but semi-solid-state cells could reach deployment faster than pure solid-state while still improving on lithium-ion.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Near-term semi-solid-state deployment is likelier than all-solid-state for Chinese battery makers.
insights.quote: Lab results in battery research are notoriously difficult to scale
insights.locator: China is also leading innovation in key technologies

themes.theme: Data-center demand pulls in US firms

insights.claim: Only three US companies made the list, two of which got a major boost from Big Tech seeking data-center power, and the third, Brimstone, is leaning into critical minerals; technologies providing consistent power are in high demand.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Firm clean power is where AI-driven capital is flowing within US climate tech.
insights.quote: Technologies that can provide consistent power are in high demand.
insights.locator: Everybody wants a piece of the data center pie

insights.claim: Fervo Energy uses horizontal drilling and fracking to make geothermal practical in more places, raised $2.2 billion in a May IPO, and plans a gigawatt of operating plants by end of 2030.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Fervo's IPO makes it a public-market proxy for next-generation geothermal.
insights.locator: Fervo Energy is bringing next-generation geothermal

insights.claim: X-energy is building helium-cooled small modular reactors, currently a 320 MW cluster with Amazon in Richland, Washington, and has a Dow deal that could deploy one at a Dow chemical plant in the early 2030s.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: SMRs are gaining both hyperscaler and industrial-heat offtakers.
insights.locator: X-energy is building helium-cooled small modular

themes.theme: Grid storage as the key enabler

insights.claim: As solar and wind scale up, storage is needed to help them meet more of grid demand, and the storage market has exceeded the author's expectations over four years of covering it.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Storage demand growth is structurally tied to renewable build-out.
insights.quote: energy storage market has surpassed even my expectations
insights.locator: The grid needs support, and energy storage will be a key piece moving forward

insights.claim: Form Energy, on the list a third time, is planning a 30 GWh iron-air battery project to power a Google data center that could be the world's largest battery by capacity, coming online in phases between 2028 and 2031.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Long-duration iron-air storage gets its first gigawatt-hour-scale hyperscaler contract.
insights.locator: Form Energy is on the list for a third time

insights.claim: Energy Dome's compressed-CO2 storage is already cheaper than lithium-ion for long durations (10 hours or more), with plans for over 30 GWh of plants worldwide including one with Google in Ireland due online in 2028.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: CO2-based long-duration storage is positioned to undercut lithium-ion beyond ~10 hours.

insights.claim: About a million EV batteries are expected to reach end of life by 2030, and Moment Energy repurposes used batteries for backup power at a facility in Vancouver, British Columbia.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Second-life batteries create a secondary market as EV packs retire.
insights.locator: And Moment Energy is working to use
